newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to boost California trade ties - paper.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to boost California trade ties - paper.

text.p: Singapore wants to strengthen trade ties with the U.S. state of California in a three-pronged pact on technology, tourism and tertiary education, according to a report in Saturday's Straits Times newspaper.
The paper quoted Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Tony Tan as saying there was "a lot of scope" to promote co-operation in these areas after a meeting with visiting California governor, Pete Wilson.
No firm commercial agreements had been made, but Wilson was quoted as agreeing that "the opportunities for joint ventures, I think, are extremely great".
California is the largest exporter to Singapore of all U.S. states. It is also one of the largest investors.
It is likely that any initiative would be examined under the Singapore-United States Business Council, which Tan chairs.
The council groups 10 top U.S. firms, which have invested more than Singapore $7 billion in the island republic, with 10 of Singapore's business leaders.
